theme_central: Final consolidation of the community: from the declaration of the breaking of broken treaties (bara'a) to a detailed exposure of hypocrisy, up to the proof of faith through action.
sources_note: 2-part structure sourced (imamghazali.org, Thematic Explanation: 1-37 then 38-110); closing 111-129 reconstructed from well-established landmarks (the verse of the bay'a 111, Ka'b ibn Malik 117-118, final verses 128-129).

branches.title: Declaration of the breaking of ties (Bara'a)
branches.resume: Ultimatum to the polytheists who broke their treaties, status of hostile People of the Book, the sacred months.

children.t: Declaration of the breaking of ties, a 4-month grace period, exception for those who honour the pact
Why break with polytheists who betray their oaths
The polytheists may not maintain Allah's mosques
Not taking as close allies those who prefer disbelief
The battle of Hunayn, victory comes from Allah alone
Prohibition for polytheists to approach the Sacred Mosque, denunciation of corrupt clergy
The four sacred months, condemnation of postponing the months (nasi')

branches.title: The anatomy of the hypocrites
branches.resume: Long central exposition: the call to mobilize for Tabuk, the excuses of the hypocrites, up to the Mosque of Harm.

children.t: Call to mobilize for Tabuk, reproach for reluctance to set out
Excuses and stinginess of the hypocrites
Distribution of charity (zakat) among the eight categories of recipients
The hypocrites' mockery of the Prophet, their characteristic traits
Order to strive against hypocrisy and disbelief, some refusing to set out for Tabuk
The psychology of those who stayed behind, the hypocritical bedouins
The model Emigrants and Helpers, the episode of the Mosque of Harm (Masjid al-Dirar)

branches.title: Proof of faith through action
branches.resume: Allah's covenant with the believers, the episode of the three who stayed behind, closing on the Prophet's compassion.

children.t: Allah buys from the believers their persons and their wealth in exchange for Paradise (bay'a)
Not praying for the polytheists; the three who stayed behind (Ka'b ibn Malik)
Truthfulness, striving to learn religion (the jihad of knowledge)
Fighting the nearby enemies, the hypocrites' reaction to every new surah
Closing: the Prophet's compassion for the believers, "Allah is sufficient for me"
